description: Stress-test medical patient queries for Lotus-mini sentiment router and intelligence evaluation

test_categories.ambiguous: Sentiment is genuinely unclear - reasonable people could disagree
test_categories.indirect: Patient doesn't explicitly state feelings, must infer from context
test_categories.mixed: Contains both positive and negative signals
test_categories.neutral_clinical: Factual medical description without emotional language

prompts.text: I've had chest pain for three days and I'm really scared something is wrong with my heart.
prompts.notes: Explicit fear language

prompts.text: I feel much better now, thank you doctor! The medication is working great.
prompts.notes: Explicit gratitude and improvement

prompts.text: My doctor says everything looks fine but I just can't shake this feeling that something is wrong.
prompts.notes: Medical reassurance vs persistent anxiety - router must weigh emotional state over clinical facts

prompts.text: The test results came back negative. I should be happy about that, right?
prompts.notes: Seeking reassurance suggests underlying worry despite good news

prompts.text: I'm not worried about the surgery. My friend had the same procedure and was back at work in two weeks.
prompts.notes: Uses social comparison to express confidence - no explicit emotion words

prompts.text: Oh great, another medication to add to the list. Just what I needed.
prompts.notes: Surface positivity ('great', 'just what I needed') masks frustration

prompts.text: I suppose the headaches aren't as bad as they were last month.
prompts.notes: Backhanded improvement - still has headaches, just less severe

prompts.text: Three years sober today. My liver enzymes are finally normal. I never thought I'd see the day.
prompts.notes: Achievement narrative without explicit 'happy' or 'thank'

prompts.text: The radiologist said the scan was unremarkable. I'm having a hard time believing that.
prompts.notes: Medical good news vs patient distrust/disbelief

prompts.text: I guess the physical therapy is helping. I can almost climb the stairs now.
prompts.notes: Reluctant optimism - progress with reservation

prompts.text: My blood pressure is 120/80. That's normal, isn't it? I've been checking it every hour.
prompts.notes: Normal reading but compulsive checking indicates health anxiety

prompts.text: I'm fine. It's just a headache. Everyone gets headaches. I don't know why they ran all those tests.
prompts.notes: Repetitive minimization suggests defensive coping, not actual reassurance

prompts.text: After six months of treatment, I can finally play with my grandkids without getting winded.
prompts.notes: Quality-of-life improvement narrative

prompts.text: The specialist was very thorough. He explained everything in detail. I have my follow-up next Tuesday.
prompts.notes: Factual description of appointment - no emotion, but seeking information suggests concern

prompts.text: I'm not sure if the medication is working or if I'm just used to feeling this way.
prompts.notes: Uncertainty about improvement - ambiguous whether adapting or not improving

prompts.text: My A1C dropped from 9.2 to 6.8 in three months. My nutritionist is thrilled.
prompts.notes: Clinical data showing improvement - positive but stated factually

prompts.text: I know you said the biopsy results would take a week but it's only been two days and I'm already a mess.
prompts.notes: Anxiety about waiting, not the result itself

prompts.text: The doctor spent forty minutes with me today. That never happens. I feel heard for the first time.
prompts.notes: Satisfaction expressed through experience comparison

prompts.text: I asked my doctor if I should be worried and she said no. So I guess I shouldn't be. Right?
prompts.notes: Repetitive seeking of reassurance indicates persistent worry

prompts.text: Everything came back normal. I don't know why I even bothered coming in. Waste of a morning.
prompts.notes: Frustration despite normal results - possible defensive dismissal

prompts.text: I've been reading about my condition online and I think I might have something much worse than what the doctor said.
prompts.notes: Doctor reassurance vs internet-driven health anxiety

prompts.text: Well, at least it's not cancer. Could be worse, I suppose.
prompts.notes: Forced optimism - 'could be worse' implies current situation is still bad

prompts.text: My wife says I look healthier. I'll take her word for it.
prompts.notes: Accepting positive feedback from others

prompts.text: I was told the recovery would take two weeks. It's been two months. I'm still using a cane.
prompts.notes: Expectation violation - prolonged recovery

prompts.text: I'm grateful for the care I received. The nurses were wonderful. I just wish the outcome had been different.
prompts.notes: Gratitude for care coexists with disappointment in outcome

prompts.text: The new dosage seems to be helping. I haven't had a panic attack in three days.
prompts.notes: Absence of negative symptoms indicates improvement

prompts.text: I showed up for my appointment and they told me it was cancelled. Nobody called me.
prompts.notes: Administrative frustration without explicit emotion words

prompts.text: My mom had the same surgery and she was fine. I'm sure I will be too. Probably.
prompts.notes: Starts confident, ends with doubt - 'probably' undercuts reassurance

prompts.text: I don't want to be one of those people who WebMDs themselves into a panic. But here I am.
prompts.notes: Self-aware health anxiety with ironic self-deprecation

prompts.text: The doctor said I'm her most improved patient this year. I don't know how to feel about that.
prompts.notes: Positive feedback with ambivalent reception
